content:
maya: Thinking out loud — proposing a long-lived refactor RFC: split the monolithic "helix" runtime into three narrow modules (ingest, core-exec, telem) and introduce a thin orchestration facade. Goal is easier independent deploys, targeted SLOs, and smaller ownership surfaces.

sam: 👍 curious about the migration path. do we do a big bang cutover or incremental?

maya: incremental. plan sketch: 1) extract read-only interfaces and tests, 2) compile a compatibility shim, 3) route a subset of traffic to the new modules behind feature flags, 4) ramp and retire old paths.

chris: how do we handle KV cache ownership? that was the biggest pain last time.

maya: keep cache in core-exec initially, expose a narrow RPC for prefix hints. later we can move ownership when we’re confident. avoids heavy cross-service transactions during cutover.

raj: observability concerns: we need end-to-end traceability before routing. otherwise debugging will be hell. recommend a canary pipeline that enforces full tracing and latency histograms.

kelly: from product side, timelines are flexible but we need no customer-visible perf regressions. can we set a latency SLO per module and an overall budget?

maya: yes — module SLOs: ingest p50 < 15ms, core-exec p50 < 40ms, telem p99 < 200ms. overall budget <= current p50/p99. if any module breaches during ramp, auto-fallback to monolith.

sam: auto-fallback — do we use route policy in the router? I can add a circuit breaker that watches error rate + latency.

chris: also need compatibility for model kernel selection logic — that's stateful. proposal: compile kernel selection into a small library that both monolith and core-exec call; avoids behavioral drift.

maya: good point. we'll package kernel selector as an internal artifact and version it. include integration tests in CI to detect drift.

raj: DB migrations? the monolith has a few schema changes tucked away. migrating to separate modules could surface hidden assumptions.

maya: minimal migration approach: keep a single schema but introduce a service-owned namespace for new columns. use feature-flagged reads/writes. if rollback needed, writes still compatible.

sam: what about deployment cadence — modules should be able to roll independently. need per-module release windows early to catch issues.

kelly: okay — product asks for a detailed rollout plan and rollback playbook. can we scope a 6-week pilot?

maya: yes. week-by-week:
- week 0: design doc + API stubs + owners assigned
- week 1-2: extract interfaces, package kernel selector, add tracing hooks
- week 3: deploy core-exec behind flags for 5% traffic, full tracing enforced
- week 4: ramp to 25%, run performance tuning, add circuit-breaker rules
- week 5: validate telemetry & rollback drills, ramp to 60%
- week 6: full cutover for non-critical tenants, start deprecating monolith paths

sam: sounds reasonable. we should reserve a gate for SRE/observability signoff at the end of week 3 and week 5.

raj: I'll draft the observability gating checklist: traces, latency histograms, tail-latency mitigation, error budgets, synthetic tests.

chris: security note — facade must still enforce tenant isolation and auth. no plaintext IPCs. we need mTLS and short-lived tokens between modules.

maya: agreed. include mTLS + token rotation in the security workstream. also KMS access for any new module secrets.

kelly: dependencies: this touches runtime, router, infra for mTLS, and deploy tooling. I'll coordinate cross-team blockers.

deploy-bot: deployment: core-exec:canary started for 5% traffic on cluster-2 (job id: deploy-1768130001) :rocket:

sam: thanks — next steps: finalize RFC this week, assign owners, SRE to create gating checklist, infra to scope mTLS work. I'll create the follow-up ticket list.

maya: tagging @raj @chris for the checklists. anything else?

raj: I'll post the observability checklist PR in #eng-sre tomorrow.

chris: I'll start the kernel-selector packaging spike; aim to land by EOD Fri.

kelly: I'll add the rollout calendar to the program board and flag customers that need early outreach.

maya: great. thanks all. we'll reconvene after week 1 for a quick sync. :thumbsup:
